summary: On April 25, 2024 a marketing employee at Singapore jerky retailer Bee Cheng Hiang sent bulk marketing emails using a Python script generated with a generative AI tool. The prompt did not tell the tool to hide recipients, and the script put every address in each batch of up to 1,000 into the visible To field, exposing the email addresses of 95,364 members to each other. Testing only checked activity logs, so the error was missed. The company stopped the emails and notified Singapore's PDPC on April 27; the PDPC called it Singapore's first AI-related data breach and accepted a voluntary undertaking.
